order: Address two findings raised during the latest review pass. First, creation-time identity capture must never degrade to a lexical guess: checkout creation determines the canonical path itself and refuses the checkout, with the registration cleaned up, whenever that lookup fails; the lexical fallback serves paths that are already gone through sweeping, not the general case. Lock in a regression for a poisoned-real-path scenario and confirm it fails without the fix. Second, both review-lane kill branches poll git's actual registration lock rather than sleeping a fixed duration — a slow checkout can remain locked past any fixed delay, so a duration-based sleep does not hold up here. Also correct the continuous-integration records: name the actual pull-request-head run rather than a generic label, and record the superseded run's true outcome in full, including the flake that fired during that run.
claims: Creation-time identity capture no longer degrades to a lexical guess: checkout creation determines the canonical path itself and refuses the checkout, with registration cleaned up, when that lookup fails, and a poisoned-real-path regression is pinned. Both review-lane kill branches now poll the actual registration lock instead of sleeping a fixed duration. The records were corrected to name the true pull-request-head run and the superseded run's real outcome. Verifier landed on 99 passed; registry and router held clean too, and review-lane cleared both of its runs.
